chunks.title: App shell, design tokens, shared UI kit and utilities
focus: Root layout: providers, fonts, metadata, analytics, global CSS; what wraps every page
Design tokens: every colour, radius, shadow and font defined in globals.css, lib/formStyles.ts, lib/animations.ts - list them, this feeds the UI redesign
The shadcn/base-ui component kit in components/ui: which primitives exist, which are customised, which are unused (grep usage counts)
Layout components (header, footer, nav, mobile nav) and common components; how navigation is built and where menu items are defined
Shared hooks and contexts: what state is global, how auth/profile context is provided
lib root utilities: firebase.ts vs admin-firebase.ts vs firebase-admin-rest.ts (client vs server SDK boundaries), config.ts, constants.ts, rate-limit.ts, i18n entry
proxy.ts / middleware behaviour and next.config.ts settings (images, headers, redirects, experimental flags)
Client/server component split conventions actually followed vs the documented Server-Components-first rule

chunks.title: Public site - home and information pages
focus: The home page: exact section order, each section's component, where its content comes from (Firestore collection, Supabase table, static data/ file, hardcoded)
Component tree for every page in this chunk: Page -> sections -> leaf components -> hooks/services
Which pages are Server Components and which are client; what is fetched at request time vs statically
Events and gallery: listing, detail, filtering, media handling (next/image? raw img? Firebase Storage URLs? Vercel Blob?)
Search and recommendations: how they work end to end
Framer-motion usage: which components animate and how heavily (matters for React Native)
Visual inventory for the redesign: card styles, hero patterns, section headers, spacing, typography choices actually used in these pages
Dead or duplicate pages (e.g. pages/notifications vs notifications, pages/settings vs profile/settings)

chunks.title: Public site - devotional content, bookings, donations and member pages
focus: Seva booking flow end to end: browse -> select -> book -> pay? -> receipt; which steps exist, which are stubs; where payment is (or is not) integrated
Donation flow: form, validation (zod/react-hook-form), success/failure pages, what is persisted and where
Profile, favorites, preferences, settings: what a logged-in devotee can do; how auth gates these pages
Quotes, shlokas, stotras, aaradhane public pages: data source and rendering
Public calendar (ekadashi, festivals) and knowledge base pages: data source, component tree
Temple explorer, display and QR pages: what they are for and how they work
Public AI page (app/(public)/ai) - entry point only; the engine is another chunk (M08) - note the boundary
Component tree per page; server vs client; forms and validation patterns; portability notes for each

chunks.title: Authentication, users, roles and security rules
focus: Login, register, forgot-password flows; Firebase Auth vs Supabase Auth - which is live, which is being migrated to (the repo has both)
Role model: how admin is determined (custom claims? Firestore field? env list?), set-role and create-admin API routes, and how admin routes are protected (middleware, layout check, per-page check)
Firestore and Storage security rules: summarise every rule, flag anything world-writable or inconsistent with the service layer
Session handling: cookies, tokens, server-side verification in API routes
Admin user management pages and their API
Security faults with evidence: secrets in code, unauthenticated admin APIs, client-side-only auth checks, rate limiting gaps
Portability: which auth pieces are web-only (cookies, redirects) and what a React Native client would need

chunks.title: Admin console - shell, dashboard, CRUD framework and settings
focus: Admin shell: layout, sidebar/nav definition (where menu entries live), auth gate, responsive behaviour
Dashboard: every widget, its data source and service
The generic CRUD framework (components/admin/crud, useCrudTable, crud-columns): how a new admin module is supposed to be built; which admin pages use it and which reinvent it
Settings: all 16 settings sub-pages - what each edits, which collection/document it writes, and which public page consumes it
Website-settings vs settings: overlap and confusion
Reports module and API
Test/debug pages that should not ship (admin/test, admin/test-firebase, app/debug)
Admin UI patterns actually in use (tables, forms, modals, toasts - sonner vs react-hot-toast both installed) for the redesign

chunks.title: Admin console - content, events, gallery, media and library
focus: Gallery admin has create, new, edit, edit/[id], [id]/edit and media routes - map which are live, which are duplicates or dead, and which the nav links to
Media upload pipeline: Firebase Storage vs Vercel Blob vs local public/ assets; the storage.service and api/storage routes; size/type validation
Events admin: create/edit forms, validation, publish flow, revalidation of public pages
Rich text: tiptap usage - where, how content is stored (HTML? JSON?), how it is rendered publicly (sanitisation?)
Quotes, testimonials, shlokas, stotras, announcements, temple-areas admin: data source (Firestore vs Supabase) per module
Content and library pages: what they manage
Component tree per admin page and the form patterns used; faults such as duplicated forms, missing validation, unhandled errors

chunks.title: Admin console - sevas, bookings, poojas, aaradhane, donations, billing, receipts, calendar
focus: Seva catalogue admin vs seva-bookings vs bookings: three modules - what each manages, and whether they overlap
Booking lifecycle from the admin side: statuses, transitions, who can change them, notifications
Billing and receipts: receipt creation, numbering, PDF generation (pdf-lib), printing route, email sending (nodemailer), QR codes; receipt-sevas settings
Donations admin: listing, detail, reconciliation; is there any payment gateway or is it manual
Pooja and aaradhane admin: forms, schedules, generator hand-off (the generator engine itself is chunk M14 - note the boundary)
Admin calendar (ekadashi, festivals) editing and how it feeds the public calendar
Faults: money handling (floating point, currency), missing server-side validation, missing authorization on API routes, race conditions in numbering

chunks.title: Raya AI - retrieval engine, intents, prompts, provider and chat API
focus: The request path of one chat message: API route -> intent detection -> retrieval (which sources, in which order) -> prompt composition -> LLM provider -> response -> logging/analytics. Write it as a numbered flow with file:line
Which LLM provider(s) and models are used, where keys come from, fallbacks, timeouts, cost controls
Knowledge sources: Firestore collections, Supabase tables, static files - what is retrieved and how ranked; the 'hybrid retrieval' claim vs reality
Intent system, language detection (Kannada/English?), conversation memory, unknown-question logging
AI settings: which behaviours are configurable at runtime and where they are stored
Analytics: latency, token usage, intent distribution - how measured and stored
Faults: prompt injection surface, unauthenticated AI endpoints, unbounded token spend, PII in logs; where the docs contradict the code
Portability: the engine is server-side - what a React Native client needs from it (API contract)

chunks.title: Raya AI - chat UI, admin AI console, knowledge workflow and AI UAT
focus: The chat widget/component tree on the public side: how it mounts, streams or polls, renders markdown, handles errors, mobile behaviour
Every admin/ai sub-page (analytics, health, intents, knowledge, playground, prompts, settings, testimonials, training, unknown-questions, volunteers): purpose, data source, API used
Knowledge workflow: drafts -> approvals -> versions -> publish; audit trail; comments; which collection/table each step writes
Prompt management and publishing: versioning, who can publish, how the engine picks the live prompt
AI UAT suite: what it tests, how it runs in CI, what the AI_UAT.md report claims vs what the tests assert
Faults: duplicated knowledge routes (api/knowledge vs api/admin/knowledge vs api/ai/knowledge), missing auth, UI/engine contract mismatches
Portability of the chat UI to React Native

chunks.title: Service layer and type catalogue - the repository pattern as built
focus: One table row per service file: name, backing store (Firestore collection / Supabase table / both / none), client or server SDK, exported functions, which app code imports it (grep), lines
One table row per types file: main types exported, which services and components use them
The 'no direct Firebase calls outside services' rule: grep app/ components/ hooks/ for direct firebase/firestore/supabase imports and list every violation with file:line
Client-side Firestore reads vs server-side admin SDK: which services do which, and where the SDK boundary leaks (server-only imports in client components or vice versa)
Duplicate or overlapping services (dashboard vs dashboard.client, temple-areas vs temple-areas.supabase, seva vs sevaBooking vs billing) and dead services (no importers)
Error handling, caching and pagination conventions actually used
Portability: which services could be shared with a React Native app as-is, which are tied to the Next server runtime

chunks.title: Data model, Firestore/Supabase persistence, rules, indexes, seeds and the Supabase migration
focus: Collection catalogue: every Firestore collection referenced anywhere in services/ app/ scripts/ (grep collection( and doc( names), with the fields the code reads and writes, and the docs/DATA-MODEL.md claim beside it - mark mismatches
Supabase schema from the migrations: every table, its columns, RLS policies; which Firestore collection it replaces; and whether the app code actually reads it yet

Migration state: for each domain (core, sevas, bookings, AI, content, settings, temple areas) - Firestore only / dual / Supabase only, with evidence. Note migration files whose date stamps fall after 2026-09-19
Indexes vs the queries the code runs: missing composite indexes
Seed and import scripts: what each populates, whether they are idempotent, whether they target prod
Static data in data/*.ts: what is still served from static files instead of the database
Risks: rules vs service mismatch, secrets handling (.firebase-adminsdk.json), quota issues noted in CLAUDE.md, data duplication between stores

chunks.title: API routes and server actions - the full HTTP surface
focus: One table row per route file: path, HTTP methods, auth check (none / session / admin), input validation (zod? none?), service called, store touched, response shape, caching/revalidate settings. Cover all route files - the row count must match the file count
Group routes by domain and mark duplicates and inconsistencies (e.g. api/knowledge vs api/admin/knowledge vs api/ai/knowledge; api/temple-areas vs api/admin/temple-areas)
Unauthenticated write endpoints, endpoints that seed or mutate data (seed-ai-settings, quotes/seed), debug endpoints - list them as findings
Rate limiting: where lib/rate-limit is applied and where not
Error handling and response conventions; runtime (edge vs node) per route
This table is the API contract a React Native app would consume - note gaps (no list endpoint for X, page-only data fetching with no API)

chunks.title: Device capabilities, notifications, location, QR, share, i18n and offline/PWA behaviour
focus: lib/device: every capability module (actions, calendar, capabilities, hooks, location, notifications, permissions, qr, share, settings) - what browser API it wraps, permission flow, fallbacks, and where it is used in the app
Push notifications: web push? FCM? how tokens are stored; service worker presence and what it does
PWA: manifest, icons, install prompt, offline caching - what exists in public/ and what is missing (list public/ by type, do not open images)
i18n: languages supported (Kannada? English? Sanskrit?), how strings are stored and switched, fonts for Kannada script, gaps (hardcoded strings count)
Accessibility hooks and reduced-motion handling
Device analytics and UX telemetry: what is collected and where it goes
Portability: this chunk is the closest thing to a native layer - for each capability say the React Native / Expo equivalent and how much of the current code is reusable

chunks.title: Domain engines - Panchanga calendar and festivals, Aaradhane generator, receipt PDFs, proof reports
focus: Panchanga: how the 730 daily JSON files in data/panchanga are generated (Python scripts, GitHub workflow), their schema (open two or three, never all), how the app reads them (cache, API, component), date range covered and what happens when it runs out
Festival and Ekadashi logic: static vs computed, admin-editable overrides
Aaradhane generator: inputs, algorithm, outputs, the GitHub workflow, how results reach the site
Receipt engine: PDF layout code, fonts (Kannada?), QR, numbering, email; where it runs (server route) and its dependencies
Proof reports and lib/reports: what they generate and for whom; the reports/ folder contents
Python + TypeScript split: which parts of the system are not JavaScript at all
Portability: which engines are pure logic reusable in React Native and which depend on Node/Python/server

chunks.title: Testing, CI/CD, deployment, tooling, project history and documentation health
focus: Test inventory: unit (tests/unit), functional, e2e (36 specs), ai-uat; what each file covers; which app modules have zero tests. Do not read every spec fully - list, sample, grep for describe/test names
Test runners and configs: jest, playwright, the Python report generators, shell runners - which are current and which are abandoned
CI/CD: each GitHub workflow - trigger, steps, secrets needed, what deploys where; Vercel config; Lighthouse budgets
Project history: reconstruct the timeline and scope from the root reports, sprint docs, roadmap and changelog (dates absolute; today is 2026-09-19). What was planned vs what exists
Documentation health: for each of the 27 docs/ files and 12 root reports - one line: current / partially stale / stale / empty, with one piece of evidence. CHANGELOG.md and DEPLOYMENT.md are 0 bytes
Tooling debris: .continue, .openhands, fix_lint.sh, fix-websocket.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo committed, postman collection - what to keep
Analytics and page views: what is tracked, where stored, the page_views quota issue
Build health as far as static inspection allows (node_modules is NOT installed and must not be installed): eslint config, tsconfig strictness, next.config flags that suppress errors

chunks.title: New since 2026-09-19 - the Expo mobile app, the Prisma layer, the .ai autonomous loop and the new root reports
focus: apps/mobile: stack (Expo? React Native version, router, styling), every screen and its component tree, which web API routes or services it calls, auth approach, what it shares with the web app (types? packages?) and what it duplicates - compare with docs/rearchitecture/REACT-NATIVE-MIGRATION-AND-FAULTS.md section 4 Option B and say where reality matches or departs
prisma/schema.prisma and migrations: every model, which Supabase table it mirrors, which app code uses @prisma/client (grep), whether Prisma replaced the Supabase client or sits beside it
The .ai/ folder: what the autonomous loop does (scripts, prompts, schemas, state), how it is triggered (GitHub workflow?), what it is allowed to change, risks
The new root reports: one line each - what it claims, date, whether the code agrees
Faults: new security or architecture issues these areas introduce, with path:line
Portability: what the mobile app still lacks versus the report portability matrix
